overall: The AG found the Chair and one Committee member deliberated outside a public meeting by emailing opinions to a quorum, ordered future compliance and release of the emails, and declined the spouse-sharing issue.

allegations.summary: The Chair emailed all Committee members a written response giving his opinion on a video about buffer zones and the Committee's debate before the next meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Although Chair Sweitzer asks that the video and his reply be discussed at the next meeting, his attached reply effectively let other Committee members know his opinion of the video and the underlying debate ahead of the next meeting.

allegations.summary: A Committee member replied to all members that the video was concerning and disturbing, allegedly expressing an opinion outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: communicates Ms. Tucker’s opinion on the matter, thereby taking sides in the underlying debate on issues before the Committee.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair shared Committee emails with his spouse, who is not a Committee member.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not address the issue of whether public body members may share information about Committee business with their spouses or others who are not members of the Committee.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Release to the public, within 30 days of receipt of the determination, the February 11, 2019 emails from the Chair and the Committee member, including attachments.
remedy_passage: We also order that the Committee release to the public, within 30 days following its receipt of this determination, the February 11, 2019, emails from Chair Sweitzer and Ms. Tuber referenced in this letter, including attachments.
